facts.note: The nine o'clock watch check and Félix's watch reading (twenty minutes to nine) match. The scolding is attributed to 'my husband', and the transcript never explicitly identifies the husband as Aurèle. 'Aurèle' appears only in the next sentence ('Aurèle knew that. He could not resist.'), so 'Aurèle scolded him' is not stated outright.
When the temple struck ten, she looked at the salon clock, which showed five minutes to ten.
She and the doctor (Casimir) played piquet in the salon without a break until he went out for cigars at twenty-eight minutes past ten by the salon clock.
As he went out he asked her to play for him; she sat at the piano at once, played until he came back, and stopped when he came in.
A moment after he came back, the hall clock struck eleven.
